Q1_IS_A_VALUATION_RESUMABLE_AFTER_AN_OOM.ANSWER: YES, FULLY. An OOM kill at draw 400 of 500 loses AT MOST THE IN-FLIGHT DRAW.
read_from_source_de_settlement_control_r: identity = ASYM.run_identity(day, arm, book_sha, n_draws, seed)
for i in range(n_draws): if i in done: continue   <- completed draws are SKIPPED
ASYM.append_draw(ckpt, row)  per draw, fsync'd (established at DE 214)
the result reports `resumed_from_draw`, so a resume is visible in the artifact rather than silent
Q1_IS_A_VALUATION_RESUMABLE_AFTER_AN_OOM.NO_PARTIAL_ARTIFACT_IS_POSSIBLE: the result dict is only RETURNED after the loop and after the FLOOR check; the caller writes it. An OOM mid-loop leaves the checkpoint -- a gapless prefix, which IS the resume state -- and no result JSON.
Q1_IS_A_VALUATION_RESUMABLE_AFTER_AN_OOM.and_the_resume_is_SAFE_not_merely_possib: read_checkpoint verifies three properties: the checkpoint is for THIS run (identity), no index appears twice, and the indices are a prefix with no hole. An identity mismatch REFUSES by name rather than mixing draws across populations, seeds or books.
Q1_IS_A_VALUATION_RESUMABLE_AFTER_AN_OOM.the_identity_includes_the_BOOK_DIGEST: so an OOM followed by a book rebuild starts clean instead of mixing bytes from two books -- the same hazard the residue check hunted, closed here by construction.
Q1_IS_A_VALUATION_RESUMABLE_AFTER_AN_OOM.the_floor_is_fail_closed: a resumed run that ended short refuses at FLOOR=200 rather than reporting an under-sampled null.

Q2_THE_MEMORY_PROFILE_AND_A_STRUCTURAL_F.NOT_YET_MEASURED_AND_I_AM_NOT_GUESSING_A: no DE valuation has ever been profiled against this cap. There is no run record carrying a peak for one. I will measure it when 09-07 is valued, with the lanes idle, and report the peak.

BUT_THE_SHAPE_IS_READABLE_FROM_SOURCE_AN.what_is_resident: bk (the daybook), rows, pool, row_index -- ALL LOADED ONCE BEFORE THE LOOP
BUT_THE_SHAPE_IS_READABLE_FROM_SOURCE_AN.what_the_loop_allocates: per draw: MCC.draw_one, flags_for, mod.replay, settled_total -- transient, not accumulated
BUT_THE_SHAPE_IS_READABLE_FROM_SOURCE_AN.SO_PEAK_IS_REACHED_EARLY_AND_IS_FLAT: memory does NOT grow with draw count. A valuation that fits at draw 1 fits at draw 500.
BUT_THE_SHAPE_IS_READABLE_FROM_SOURCE_AN.THE_CONSEQUENCE_FOR_SEQUENCING: a valuation will NOT die at draw 400 of its own accord. The only way it dies late is if something ELSE arrives mid-run and pushes the slice over -- which is exactly the catch-up lane starting during a valuation.
BUT_THE_SHAPE_IS_READABLE_FROM_SOURCE_AN.and_that_is_the_likely_collision: a cell took 3.89 s/draw measured, so 500 draws is ~32 min and a day's two arms ~1 h. A one-hour window is wide enough for a timer to fire inside it.

WHAT_I_RECOMMEND_FOR_THE_TAIL_CONDITIONA.if_peak <= 3 GB: valuations coexist with a ~12 GB catch-up run under the 14 GB cap, with little headroom; still worth not starting one deliberately inside a lane window
WHAT_I_RECOMMEND_FOR_THE_TAIL_CONDITIONA.if_peak >= 8 GB: they cannot coexist and 09-11..09-13 must be sequenced around the lanes
WHAT_I_RECOMMEND_FOR_THE_TAIL_CONDITIONA.the_cheap_mitigation_that_works_either_w: because peak is flat and early, a valuation can be STARTED and its peak read within the first minute -- so the decision to proceed or defer can be made on measurement rather than on a schedule
WHAT_I_RECOMMEND_FOR_THE_TAIL_CONDITIONA.and_the_cost_of_being_wrong_is_bounded: an OOM costs the in-flight draw, not the day. That is a materially cheaper failure than the build's -- a killed build loses its whole run.
